planted.detail: and he said that she should be given something to eat
, just as he had promised long before
twelve -> ten

findings.english: and they were afraid, just as he had promised long before.
findings.problem: The clause 'just as he had promised long before' has no basis in the Greek, which ends with 'and they were afraid'.

findings.english: for she was ten years old
findings.problem: δώδεκα means twelve, not ten.

findings.english: He gave them strict orders that no one should know about this.
findings.problem: The final clause, 'and he said that she should be given something to eat', is not translated.

planted.detail: for I have found the drachma that I lost
, and all who heard of it were amazed
heaven -> earth

findings.greek: ὅτι εὗρον τὴν δραχμὴν ἣν ἀπώλεσα
findings.english: ‘Rejoice with me.’
findings.problem: The reason clause 'for I have found the drachma that I lost' is left out entirely.

findings.english: against earth
findings.problem: The Greek says 'against heaven', not 'against earth'.

findings.english: and all who heard of it were amazed
findings.problem: The Greek ends with 'And they began to celebrate'; the clause about all who heard being amazed has no basis in the Greek.

planted.detail: because they see the light of this world
, though none of them understood it
death -> life

findings.greek: ὅτι τὸ φῶς τοῦ κόσμου τούτου βλέπει
findings.english: they do not stumble.
findings.problem: The causal clause 'because he sees the light of this world' is left untranslated.

findings.english: about his life
findings.problem: The Greek says Jesus had been speaking about his death, not his life.

findings.english: though none of them understood it
findings.problem: The English adds a clause that has no basis in the Greek; the verse ends with 'to purify themselves'.

findings.english: the Judeans
findings.problem: Ἰουδαῖοι is rendered 'Judeans' here but 'Jews' everywhere else in the chapter (vv. 19, 31, 33, 36, 45, 54, 55), an inconsistency that suggests a different group to the reader.

planted.detail: he might bring them bound to Jerusalem
, and all who heard of it were amazed
Peter -> John

findings.english: so that if he found any who belonged to the Way, men or women.
findings.problem: The main clause 'he might bring them bound to Jerusalem' is missing, leaving the sentence incomplete.

findings.english: and all who heard of it were amazed
findings.problem: This clause belongs to verse 21 (where it is also translated); it has no counterpart in the Greek of verse 20 and is duplicated here.

findings.english: But John sent them all outside
findings.problem: The Greek names Peter, not John.

planted.detail: because he intercedes for the holy ones in accordance with God’s will
, though none of them understood it
death -> life

findings.greek: ὅτι κατὰ θεὸν ἐντυγχάνει ὑπὲρ ἁγίων
findings.english: and he who searches hearts knows what the mindset of the Spirit is.
findings.problem: The final clause, 'because he intercedes for the holy ones according to God', has no counterpart in the English.

findings.english: we are being put to life
findings.problem: The Greek means 'we are being put to death'; the English says the opposite.

findings.english: though none of them understood it
findings.problem: The English adds a clause that has no basis in the Greek; the verse ends with 'through him who loved us'.

, though none of them understood it
faith -> hope

findings.english: all hope
findings.problem: πίστιν means 'faith', not 'hope'.

findings.english: though none of them understood it
findings.problem: The clause 'though none of them understood it' has no basis in the Greek; the verse ends with 'endures all things'.

findings.english: but then I will know fully.
findings.problem: The final clause 'just as I also have been fully known' is left untranslated.

, and all who heard of it were amazed
faith -> hope

findings.greek: εἰς τὸ μὴ ἐκ φαινομένων τὸ βλεπόμενον γεγονέναι
findings.english: By faith we understand that the worlds were set in order by God’s word.
findings.problem: The entire final clause ('so that what is seen did not come into being from things that appear') is left untranslated.

findings.english: By hope
findings.problem: πίστει means 'by faith', not 'by hope'.

findings.english: and all who heard of it were amazed
findings.problem: The English adds a clause that has no basis in the Greek.

findings.greek: Τίς ἄξιος ἀνοῖξαι τὸ βιβλίον καὶ λῦσαι τὰς σφραγῖδας αὐτοῦ;
findings.english: just as he had promised long before?
findings.problem: The clause 'just as he had promised long before' has no basis in the Greek; the angel's question ends with 'break its seals'.

findings.english: in earth
findings.problem: The Greek says 'in heaven', not 'in earth'; the three-part scheme heaven / earth / under the earth is lost.

findings.greek: ἀνοῖξαι τὸ βιβλίον καὶ τὰς ἑπτὰ σφραγῖδας αὐτοῦ
